pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-N-Methyl-D-Aspartate Receptor (Anti-NMDAR) Encephalitis secondary to an ovarian teratoma THE SMOKING GUN: The combination of acute psychiatric onset, continuous orofacial dyskinesias, extreme delta brush on EEG, and an underlying ovarian teratoma acting as the autoimmune trigger in a young female. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: This condition is an autoimmune paraneoplastic syndrome. Ectopic neural tissue residing within an ovarian teratoma expresses functional NMDAR subunits. The immune system generates IgG antibodies against the GluN1 subunit of these receptors. These cross-reactive antibodies cross the blood-brain barrier and bind to neuronal NMDARs in the central nervous system, causing cross-linking and internalisation of the receptors. This reversible reduction of NMDAR density leads to a loss of GABAergic inhibition, precipitating a sequence of severe psychiatric symptoms, dyskinesias, autonomic lability, and central hypoventilation. Treatment requires prompt surgical resection of the teratoma alongside aggressive immunotherapy (plasma exchange, IVIG, corticosteroids, and rituximab).
